Behind the motion.

The mechanical sculpture combines watch movements and robotics, with project scenes built from the same cobalt, chrome, and enamel palette. The models are original procedural geometry built for this site. Pointer hits use raycasting and local springs; the disassembly and scroll transitions share the page's animation clock.

References

  • Lusion — the visual reference for a generous editorial layout, glossy sculptural objects, and motion that drives the page.
  • Lusion’s WebGL Scroll Sync — a reference for DOM-aligned WebGL windows and the adapted, velocity-responsive displacement shader. MIT notice.
  • 14islands’ viewport scroll scenes — the pattern for rendering neighboring art windows through one shared canvas, with a camera and scissored viewport for each frame. MIT notice.
  • Codrops’ Magnetic Buttons — damped hover response, layered label movement, and rolling text. MIT notice.
  • Lenis 1.3.11 — smooth wheel scrolling synchronized with the animation clock. MIT notice.
  • Three.js physical materials and clearcoat example — reflective cobalt, brushed metal, and enamel materials.
  • Codrops: glass and plastic in Three.js — material and lighting research for the scene.

Libraries

Three.js 0.180.0, including its RoomEnvironment and RoundedBoxGeometry, provides the renderer, procedural lighting environment, geometry, and raycasting. MIT notice. GSAP 3.13.0, ScrollTrigger, and SplitText handle the coordinated entrances, heading reveals, and project sequence. Lenis 1.3.11 synchronizes smooth wheel input with that clock; touch navigation retains native scrolling.

Typography and assets

The prototype photograph comes from our Undercity team project, using the Hack Club Blot plotter. The project's character takes inspiration from Paolo. The SkyCell dashboard replays archived APEX / SondeHub tracker data. The Marble visual is an explanatory workflow diagram, rather than a screenshot of private software.

DM Sans is served locally, including its variable weights, under the SIL Open Font License 1.1. Copyright belongs to the DM Sans Project Authors. No external font request is required to read or use the page.

The Lusion reference informed the visual direction; the public examples above informed specific implementations. This is not a claim about the libraries used by Lusion’s current site. No Lusion images, models, or production assets are reused. The sculptures require no downloaded 3D models, HDR photographs, or paid assets. Motion can be paused; reduced-motion preferences and WebGL failure retain the readable page, and small screens use a natural vertical layout.
